messages:
Anya: quick design check 1 playground streaming controls. Users hit the same button expecting to pause; we should design for keyboard-first workflows too. Figma: https://fig.ma/file/streaming-ux-kb. Thoughts on labels and token meter placement?
Mike: absolutely. For keyboard users, make Pause/Resume one toggle (Space) and make Discard a separate action (D) with confirm. Visual affordance should show a focused state when message is targetable.
Lee: propose compact inline token meter inside the message footer:  [3 tk  $0.0003]  focusable but visually muted. Default hidden unless dev mode or focused.
Tara: agree. Also propose different words: Hold / Drop / Retry to be more action-oriented. But test for clarity.
Anya: copy candidates:
```
Primary: Pause (preserves state) | Discard (clears)
Alt test: Hold | Drop
Tooltip: "Pause to preserve and resume later" / "Discard will remove partial response"
```
Mike: prefer Pause/Discard for non-dev users; Hold/Drop sounds slangy. Keep tooltips explicit.
Lee: keyboard flow: when message focused, Space toggles pause. If paused, pressing R opens a confirmation: "Discard paused response and regenerate?" Accept/Cancel. Provide aria-live updates: "Response paused" / "Response discarded".
aria-bot: accessibility checklist: provide clear aria-labels for the token meter, ensure focus ring on chip, announce state changes via polite aria-live, include keyboard shortcut help in the Help panel.
ux-bot: small visual nit: when paused show thin persistent strip under message with status + ttl: "Paused  expires in 2:59". Keep color subtle and ensure contrast.
Tara: token meter placement: inside footer avoids toolbar overcrowding. On hover/focus show estimate; mobile long-press. Keep default off for regular users.
Anya: action items: Mike to draft keyboard shortcut spec; Lee to mock compact token meter in Figma; Tara to run quick wording test Pause vs Hold; aria-bot to write a11y acceptance. I'll update the mock and link back here. Thanks! :sparkles:
